newsitem.title: USA: Small cereal company drops suit with Kellogg.
newsitem.headline: Small cereal company drops suit with Kellogg.

text.p: A small Vermont cereal company said Tuesday it dropped its lawsuit against Kellogg Co. in a dispute over "Mooseli" cereal and a chicken in overalls.
Ward Smyth, vice president of Yankee Fare Co. -- which is also known as Three Bears Co. -- said his company reached an agreement with Kellogg, the leading U.S. cereal manufacturer.
Yankee Fare sued Kellogg in September 1996, alleging monopolistic practices, Smyth said.
Battle Creek, Mich.-based Kellogg confirmed that Yankee Fare dropped its lawsuit but made no comment about the settlement.
Smyth said the dispute began over Kellogg's complaints about its Yankee Fare's "Mooseli" multigrain cereal, which Kellogg alleged was too close to its trademark Mueslix product.

Kellogg also opposed some Yankee Fare packaging that, Smyth said, included a picture of a chicken in overalls. Kellogg claimed the chicken was too similar to its trademark "Cornelius the Rooster" character used to market Kellogg's Corn Flakes, Smyth said.

Smyth said Kellogg's also opposed Yankee Fare's slogan of "It tastes just right," which Kellogg felt referred to another of its cereals, "Just Right." Smyth said the slogan was derived from the "Goldilocks and the Three Bears" fairy tale.

Smyth said that under the settlement Kellogg's will not oppose the use of Vermont Mooseli or the depiction of a chicken on its packaging of Vermont Morning Porridge. The company can use the slogan "It tastes just right" on packaging, but cannot use the phrase on business cards.
